nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of Co(OH)2
nodes.procedure: The first step involves the synthesis of Co(OH)2 nanoflowers on the carbon cloth (CC) via a one-step hydrothermal treatment of the precursor at 120°C for 6 h.
nodes.source_text: The first step involves the synthesis of Co(OH)2 nanoflowers on the carbon cloth (CC) via a one-step hydrothermal treatment of the precursor at 120°C for 6 h.

nodes.name: Electrochemical deposition and annealing
nodes.procedure: Then, the obtained Co(OH)2 nanoflower on CC was subjected to electrochemical deposition at -1.0 V vs Ag/AgCl for 20 minutes utilizing Ir and Ru precursors. Subsequently, the resulting sample was annealed at 400°C in air for 3 h to get the RuIr-Co3O4 nanoflower.

nodes.characterization_summary: RuIr-Co3O4, Ru-Co3O4, Ir-Co3O4, and Co3O4 exhibit characteristic diffraction peaks matching cobalt spinel oxide (JCPDS PDF# 74-2120) with no Ir/Ru-based oxides or impurities detected.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystal structure of RuIr-Co3O4, Ru-Co3O4, Ir-Co3O4, and Co3O4 is then examined by X-ray diffraction (XRD, Figure 1b; Figure S1, Supporting Information), which reveals characteristic diffraction peaks that match well with cobalt spinel oxide...

nodes.characterization_summary: RuIr-Co3O4 exhibits nanoflower morphology identical to Co3O4 with no apparent change after Ru and Ir doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images of RuIr-Co3O4 exhibit the same nanoflower morphology to that of Co3O4, indicating no apparent change in morphology after Ru and Ir doping...

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM image confirms RuIr-Co3O4 nanoflower has thickness of 18.3 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Together with the Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images in Figure S3 (Supporting Information), the Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) image (Figure S4, Supporting Information) confirmed that the RuIr-Co3O4 nanoflower has a thickness of 18.3 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringes with d-spacing of 0.467 nm and 0.284 nm corresponding to (111) and (220) planes of RuIr-Co3O4; lattice slightly broader (0.467 nm, 0.287 nm) than pure Co3O4 (0.46 nm) indicating successful Ru/Ir incorporation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Specifically, the HRTEM images show two lattice fringes with a d spacing of 0.467 and 0.284 nm corresponding to the (111) and (220) planes of RuIr-Co3O4 (Figure 1d), respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED confirms RuIr-Co3O4 and Co3O4 are polycrystalline with planes (111), (220), (311), (400), (422), (511), and (440) consistent with XRD.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM) images and the corresponding selected area electron diffraction (SAED) revealed that the as-synthesized Co3O4 displays a polycrystalline structure... SAED analysis confirmed that the polycrystals of Co3O4 are oriented along the (111), (220), (311), (400), (422), (511), and (440) planes...

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping confirms uniform distribution of Ru, Ir, Co, and O throughout RuIr-CO3O4 nanoflower catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The elemental mapping also confirmed the uniform distribution of Ru, Ir, Co, and O throughout the entire RuIr-CO3O4 nanoflower catalyst (Figure 1e).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS reveals Ru:Ir:Co molar ratio of 1:0.8:233 with Ru 2.7 wt% and Ir 0.25 wt% mass loading in RuIr-CO3O4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, the Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectroscopy (ICP-MS) analysis on the RuIr-CO3O4 sample unveils the molar ratio of Ru: Ir: Co is 1: 0.8: 233. And the Ru and Ir mass loading is 2.7 wt% and 0.25 wt% in the RuIr-CO3O4.

nodes.characterization_summary: Red shift of A1g band in RuIr-Co3O4, Ru-Co3O4, Ir-Co3O4 confirms lattice expansion due to Ru/Ir substitution; A1g band broadened and red-shifted indicating Ru/Ir occupy octahedral Co(III) positions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The red shift of the A1g band in the Raman spectra of RuIr-Co3O4, Ru-Co3O4, and broad Ir-Co3O4, relative to that of Co3O4, confirms lattice expansion due to Ru and Ir substitution...

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p XPS shifts to higher binding energy indicating increased Co oxidation state in RuIr-Co3O4 vs doped variants and Co3O4; O 1s deconvoluted to M-O (529.6 eV) and M-OH (531.1 eV) with M-O peak shifting lower; Ru 3d shifts higher; Ir 4f shifts lower vs IrO2 indicating reduced Ir valence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The O 1s XPS result of RuIr-Co3O4 is deconvoluted into two peaks located at 529.6 and 531.1 eV corresponding to the lattice M-O and M-OH... Besides, the Co 2p XPS of RuIr-Co3O4 exhibits a shift toward higher binding energy...

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge shifts higher indicating increased Co valence state; Ru K-edge indicates +3.4 valence; Ir L-edge between IrO2 and IrCl3 indicating valence between +3 and +4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co K-edge of RuIr-Co3O4, compared to those of Co3O4, CoO, and Co foil, shifts to higher energy, also indicating an increase in the valence state of Co in RuIr-Co3O4 due to Ru and Ir substitution...

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS shows Co-O at 1.50 Å (shorter than Co3O4 1.53 Å), Ru-O at 1.48 Å, Ir-O at 1.47 Å, Ru-Co_oct at 2.45 Å confirming Ru substitutes octahedral Co sites; reduced peak intensity indicates vacancies and disorder from Ru/Ir incorporation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The bond length of Co-O in RuIr-Co3O4 (1.50 Å) is shorter than in Co3O4 (1.53 Å) (Figure 2d), suggesting stronger covalency bond Co-O interactions...

nodes.characterization_summary: Cdl of RuIr-Co3O4 is 123.3 mF cm^-2, higher than Ru-Co3O4 (116.5 mF cm^-2), Ir-Co3O4 (76.8 mF cm^-2), and Co3O4 (0.0178 mF cm^-2).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cdl value of 123.3 mF cm^-2 is exhibited for RuIr-Co3O4, which is higher than that in Ru-Co3O4 (116.5 mF cm^-2), Ir-Co3O4 (76.8 mF cm^-2), and Co3O4 (0.0178 mF cm^-2)...

nodes.evidence_snippet: The RuIr-Co3O4 sample shows lower charge transfer resistance (Rct) of 4.5 Ω compared with other doped variants of Ru-Co3O4 (30.9 Ω), Ir-Co3O4 (42 Ω), Co3O4 (44.8 Ω), and IrO2 (10.1 Ω)...
